transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-10-05 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: see metadata above

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on POC success criteria (KPIs: p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, correctness/regressions), workload sizing, initial benchmark plan, and constraints that push their decision between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. Security/compliance and timeline (pilot week mid-Oct) are primary gating items.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria and SLOs
- Workload shape and token burn
- Benchmark design and data sharing
- Deployment tradeoffs and gating items (SLA, data residency, KMS)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam O'Connor (AE): All right, everyone we are on the hour thanks for joining. Quick intros then we will dive into what success looks like for the POC.
[00:18] Aaron Delgado (CTO): Hi, Aaron from Seraphim. We're mainly here to validate that inference cost and latency meet our product SLOs before we commit to dedicated capacity or an on-prem option.
[00:28] Priya Patel (SE): Great — I'm Priya, will be running the benchmarks and the engineering touch point. Marcus is on for deeper runtime tuning.
[00:36] Nina Roh (Lead ML Eng): Nina — I'll own model fidelity checks, we'll share a few prompt sets.
[00:40] [laughter / crosstalk]
[01:05] Priya: To set expectations, the POC we propose is two parallel tracks: a quick hosted run to validate correctness and latency at small scale, and then a Dedicated-run benchmark to validate throughput/cost at target concurrency. If required we'll scope Private/VPC tests after those.
[01:25] Tamara Voss (Security): Quick flag — our compliance team needs KMS integration details, audit log retention windows, and proof of SOC 2 before we can move data off our VPC.
[01:40] Rosa Kim (CS): We'll include the SOC2 artifacts in the security pack, Tamara. Also notes on retention and RBAC.
[01:50] Eli Santos (Platform): Do you have a timeline? When do you need results to make a decision?
[01:55] Benji Park (Product): We are aiming to decide by end of month — so a two-week POC window fits, ideally pilot starts mid October.
[02:10] Liam: Perfect. So success criteria — list what you care about. We'll call these hard SLOs vs soft success signals.
[02:17] Aaron: Hard SLOs: p99 latency under 450ms for single prompt (token length ~150 avg), and steady-state throughput of 200 requests per second for our synchronous endpoint with 8 concurrent users per instance. Cost target: total inference spend under $1,200 per 1M tokens (ballpark) — that's an internal target, open to see Redwood numbers.
[02:45] Nina: Soft signals: no more than 5% token-level degradation vs our internal baseline, deterministic outputs for canonical prompts, and easy rollback in case of regressions.
[03:00] Priya: Noted. For p99 450ms we need to confirm model size and quantization. Are you planning to use a 13B open model or a tuned 7B?
[03:12] Nina: We'll start with a tuned 7B; if things look good we might test a 13B variant. The 7B is our prod-ish model with some fine-tuning.
[03:22] Marcus Li (Solutions Eng): With a 7B we can usually hit sub-500ms on NVLink connected A100-style GPUs with batching disabled, but that depends on sequence length and KV cache behavior. If you do heavy context windows and long histories, batching helps throughput but can bump latency.
[03:45] Aaron: Our average sequence is 150 tokens, peak 600 tokens on some workflows. Token burn estimate 10M tokens/month for the first quarter post-launch.
[03:58] Priya: Good. For benchmarking we'll ask for a representative sample of prompt traces — anonymized — so that we can replay realistic distributions. We'll also provide a harness that measures p50/p95/p99 and cost per token under different batch settings.
[04:20] Tamara: Regarding data flow — we cannot send PII off-network. We'll provide a sanitized trace but may need to run Private tests if anything looks sensitive.
[04:32] Liam: Understood. So for tradeoffs: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and easier canarying, Dedicated gives predictable capacity and lower unit cost at scale, and Private is necessary when data residency/compliance prevents any egress. We'll map those to your gating criteria.
[04:56] Benji: Can you quantify the cost delta between hosted and dedicated? We want ballpark today.
[05:03] Liam: Ballpark: for a 10M token/month workload on a 7B, hosted tends to be higher by ~20-40% due to multitenant overhead; Dedicated can drop unit cost depending on utilization — at 70% utilization you'll see better economics. We'll give a spreadsheet after we see the exact prompt distribution.
[05:25] Nina: How quickly can you spin up a Dedicated pool for the POC?
[05:32] Marcus: We can provision a small dedicated pool within 48-72 hours for a POC if you sign the pilot contract and provide network peering details for Private options. For Private/VPC we need more time for orchestration — typically 2–3 weeks depending on customer network approvals.
[05:50] Eli: For Private, what's the KMS story? We use AWS KMS + our HSM. Integration is essential.
[05:58] Priya: We support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can also integrate but needs additional compliance checks. We'll include the HSM/KMS integration notes in the security pack.
[06:14] [00:06:14 timestamp — short pause as someone shares screen]
[06:40] Priya: Let's walk through the benchmark plan. Step one: hosted functional run to validate model fidelity and rough latency. Step two: dedicated benchmark for throughput and cost with your real prompt distribution. We'll run each for 48 hours to capture diurnal load.
[06:58] Aaron: For the dedicated run, what's the exact measurement approach? Do you run synthetic concurrency or replay traces?
[07:06] Priya: We do both — replay traces for fidelity and a synthetic ramp to push concurrency while observing p99 and GPU utilization. We will test batching levels: no batching (lowest latency), small batching (max 8), and aggressive batching. We'll also test quantized and FP16 paths if available.
[07:26] Marcus: Also will record KV cache hit rates; some of the tail latencies are dominated by cache warmups.
[07:35] Nina: We'll provide canonical test prompts and a golden-run baseline. We expect Redwood to run the same prompts to compare.
[07:43] Liam: Excellent. On instrumentation we'll give you token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency breakdown, and a CSV of every request with timings.
[07:53] Tamara: Do you preserve audit logs for X days? We need 180 day retention of request logs for downstream audits.
[08:02] Rosa: We can include options for extended log retention as an add-on; we'll call that out in the security docs.
[08:10] Benji: What about fallback behavior — if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can we route to Hosted?
[08:18] Marcus: Yes — smart routing supports fallback to Hosted or a cheaper model variant. We can implement automatic fallback policy in the POC to show resilience.
[08:28] Eli: For the POC, will we need to modify our client SDKs?
[08:32] Priya: Minimal — mainly endpoint changes and a small integration for the KV cache if you want prefix caching. We'll share an integration guide.
[08:40] Aaron: Timeline recap — we need results by end of month. If we start mid-Oct can this wrap up by Oct 29?
[08:46] Liam: Yes, that's feasible. Proposed schedule: 2027-10-18 hosted verification (3 days), 2027-10-21 to 10-23 dedicated benchmark, then analysis week 10-24 to 10-28 and decision 10-29.
[09:00] Nina: One question about regression testing: how do you surface model drift or output regressions during/after rolling?
[09:07] Marcus: We link the POC harness to an eval suite; we run automated quality checks comparing BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and a set of semantic checks. We can set thresholds and block rollouts if regressions exceed X%.
[09:20] Tamara: For Private, is the control plane accessible? We need no egress flows to Redwood control plane for air-gapped options.
[09:28] Priya: For on-prem/air-gapped customers we offer an offline control plane package and local telemetry ingestion. That is heavier lift and we will need network diagrams and an offline install window.
[09:41] Aaron: Ok that likely means Private is last-resort unless compliance demands it.
[09:45] Benji: How do warm-start/cold-start effects show up in p99? We care about bursty loads from our UI.
[09:52] Marcus: Cold cache warms can spike p99; we can pre-warm with KV-cache priming or keep a small hot-pool ready. We'll show that in the POC with a warmup phase.
[10:05] [Discussion of sample sizes and where to anonymize traces — Tamara emphasizes removing PII; Nina to prepare sanitized traces]
[10:38] Priya: For the initial hosted run we need a 48-hour sample of production-like prompts and a list of top 20 routes; for the dedicated run we'll need the same plus concurrency targets.
[10:50] Aaron: We can produce those by next Friday.
[10:55] Liam: Commercial — we'll send a pilot contract that covers a timeboxed dedicated pool; pricing sheet will show the delta for a month-long pilot vs ongoing reserved capacity.
[11:05] Benji: Is there a minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[11:09] Liam: For pilots we typically do a 2–4 week reserved pool with no long-term commitment. For production reserved capacity there are monthly/annual commits to get the best price. Pilot pricing is close to production but slightly higher to cover provisioning.
[11:20] Tamara: Please include the encryption at rest details and transport TLS certs in the security pack.
[11:26] Rosa: Will do.
[11:30] [wrap-up and recapitulation]
[11:31] Liam: Quick recap of action items: Priya will deliver benchmark harness and container by Oct 7, Aaron/Nina to provide sanitized traces by Oct 9, Liam to send pricing and pilot contract by Oct 6, Marcus to provide KV cache tuning notes by Oct 8, and Redwood to run hosted run and small dedicated pool on the tentative mid-Oct window.
[11:52] Aaron: Sounds good — thanks everyone. Looking forward to the harness.
[11:56] Nina: Thank you.
[11:58] Liam: We'll follow up with calendar invites and the security pack. Bye.
